# Anthony Tulk

## Overview

- **Age:** School-aged boy during the events of volumes 1–4; slightly younger than Nell Harcourt  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c20 P20](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0020)</sub>

## Appearance

Anthony is a small, dark-faced boy with keen black eyes.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P4](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0004)_

## Personality

Anthony is independent, sullen, and cheeky, with a defiant streak toward authority. He harbors a strong prejudice against female teachers, believing they are 'no good,' and shows a proud, impertinent swagger. However, he respects physical strength and firmness, eventually coming to hold Nell Harcourt in high regard after she disciplines him.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P4](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0004), [v2 c5 P10](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0010), [v2 c5 P26](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0026), [v2 c7 P5](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0005), [v2 c12 P31](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0031), [v2 c12 P52](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0052)_

## Traits

- Sullen and gloomy  <sub>[v2 c5 P4](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0004)</sub>
- Independent-minded  <sub>[v2 c7 P5](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0005)</sub>

## Abilities

- Clever student when engaged  <sub>[v2 c7 P5](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0005)</sub>

## History

Anthony Tulk, an orphaned nephew taken in by Laurence Tulk's family, enrolled in Brierley school under the instruction of Nell Harcourt. From his first day, he exhibited a sullen, defiant attitude and openly expressed his disdain for female teachers. He routinely challenged Nell's authority through subtle insolence, such as whispering, making faces, or putting a live mouse in her desk drawer. When caught placing the mouse, Nell lost her temper and whipped him with a pointer. Surprising everyone, this physical discipline won Anthony's respect, as he deemed the whipping 'just as good as a man's.' From that day on, he treated Nell with polite deference, offering to carry her books and defending her against criticism.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P0](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0000), [v2 c5 P4](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0004), [v2 c5 P26](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0026), [v2 c7 P5](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0005), [v2 c12 P23](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0023), [v2 c12 P29](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0029), [v2 c12 P33](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0033), [v2 c12 P48](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0048), [v2 c12 P50](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0050), [v2 c12 P52](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0052)_

- Orphaned nephew of Laurence Tulk, taken in to live with his family in Brierley  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045)</sub>
